# Feature: Honest Run Evidence

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-048
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_task_fidelity.md` (G4, G6, G8, G11; §5 "Changed tool contracts" and "CLI surface"; §10 FEAT-048 logging; §11 success criteria)

Make an agentic run tell the truth about itself, to the model, to the user, and to the operator, before any later feature in this plan changes behavior. Every later feature (049–053) is measured by the evidence this one repairs.

Today, run `20260925T130634Z-research-e1fd1b9d` shows the opposite:

- 11 of 22 `web_search` calls failed with a typed provider cause (`anomaly-challenge`, `empty-results`). A bare `catch {}` discarded the cause and told the model "temporarily unavailable, retryable" ([`web-search.ts:132-141`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-search.ts#L132-L141)). Nothing reached `runtime.jsonl` (121 lines, all info level).
- Our own 30-navigation budget ran out inside a search. It was recorded as the site blocking us (`reason: 'blocklist'` → stage `blocked` → a negative `blocked` rank signal), which penalized two domains in cross-run ranking ([`web-search.ts:195-199`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/web-search.ts#L195-L199), [`ranking/recording.ts:15-26`](../../../packages/core/src/ranking/recording.ts#L15-L26)).
- The published Brief had `notices: []` and `metadata.search_provider: null`, although the runtime knew both facts.
- 13 of 26 `tool-calls.jsonl` end records are unparseable strings. The Pi seam serializes the result, runs the text sanitizer, and re-parses. `URL_IN_TEXT_RE` swallows the `\` of an escaped quote, and `new URL()` normalizes it to `/` ([`event-map.ts:58-68`](../../../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/event-map.ts#L58-L68), [`strippers.ts:46`](../../../packages/core/src/sanitizer/strippers.ts#L46)). Verified on disk: `…/dallas-tx/",`.
- `usage.json` has the correct `agent` block (15 turns, $0.165) but `calls: []` and all-zero `totals`.
- No surface echoes the goal Yantra received, so a shell-expanded `$40` → `,000` goes unnoticed.

Acceptance requires all of the following:

- Every `web_search` failure carries one of `SEARCH_BLOCKED`, `SEARCH_NO_RESULTS`, `SEARCH_TIMEOUT`, `SEARCH_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, or residual `SEARCH_FAILED`, each with cause-specific wording. No two rendered messages are identical, and none advises a move the run cannot make.
- Every tool failure emits exactly one `warn` `tool_failure` line to `runtime.jsonl` with `{tool, code, cause, provider | host}` and no page text.
- A navigation/host budget refusal inside `web_search` is stage `budget`. It is reported once at the top of the result, never per site, never as stage `blocked`, and never produces a rank signal. Other URL-policy refusals (stage `policy`) produce no rank signal either.
- A published agentic Brief (agent-published, runtime-assembled, or templated) carries runtime-derived notices for every search failure cause, budget exhaustion, and per-source read failure, plus a non-null `metadata.search_provider` whenever a search ran.
- Every `tool-calls.jsonl` record re-parses as JSON, and canary secrets and PII are still redacted (property test).
- Teardown emits one `run_health` info event and writes `run-health.json`. `report.md` renders it as "Run Health".
- Agentic `usage.json` has one `calls[]` entry per provider turn, and its `totals` agree with the `agent` block whenever the provider reports per-turn usage.
- `ask`, `research`, and `do` echo the received goal on stderr, bounded and sanitized, in every mode.
- Old run directories (no `run-health.json`, empty agentic `calls`) still validate and render unchanged.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope: G4's swallowed cause (classification only), G6's budget attribution, G7's notice and `search_provider` gaps (derived from runtime facts only), G8's audit corruption, G11's usage ledger and goal echo, and the "Run health" logging contract in plan §10.

Out of scope, owned elsewhere:

- Search politeness, the challenge circuit-breaker, one provider per run, the run document cache, `limit: 0` discovery, the budget meter on results, `already_read`, and the shared browser (**FEAT-050**). FEAT-048 reports `SEARCH_BLOCKED` as non-retryable but does **not** refuse later searches; it reports repeat fetches but does **not** prevent them.
- Challenge classification of fetched pages (**FEAT-050**), page shape and links (**FEAT-051**).
- Agent-authored notices, citations by evidence ID, constraint status, and cited-versus-consulted sources (**FEAT-053**).
- The prompt's "tool retries" wording and the consecutive-failure breaker semantics (**FEAT-052**).
- The deterministic `ask`/`research --no-llm` pipelines keep their current failure handling and notices, apart from the shared `SourceFailure` stage additions they must map (TASK-004).
- Business contact redaction (plan §12 item 8, deferred).

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

No relational store. `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. This feature touches in-memory run state, three additive protocol changes, and one new run artifact.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`ToolFailureDiagnostic`** (agent, in-memory; operator-only, never model-visible). Optional `diagnostic` field on `DomainFailure`, and on `DomainSuccess` for provider/fetch-mode facts:
  - `cause` (string, closed vocabulary per tool, e.g. `anomaly-challenge`, `rate-limited`, `empty-results`, `timeout`, `key-missing`, `ethics-refused:robots`, `http-5xx`, `invalid-response`, `unexpected:<ErrorClass>`). NOT NULL on failures. Never contains a message, URL path, query, or page text.
  - `provider` (string?): search provider name when the tool used one.
  - `host` (string?): hostname only, never a full URL.
  - `fetch_mode` (`'http' | 'browser'`?): on `web_fetch` success.
- **`RunHealthLedger`** (agent, `packages/agent/src/runtime/run-health.ts`; one per run, required on `RunServices`):
  - `toolOutcomes`: ordered `{ tool, status: 'ok' | 'error' | 'timeout' | 'aborted' | 'denied', code?, cause?, provider?, host?, budgetLimit? }[]`. Recorded by the middleware for every call.
  - `sourceFailures`: ordered `{ tool, host, stage: SourceFailure['stage'], reason }[]`. Recorded by `web_search` for per-site failures.
  - `fetches`: `{ normalizedUrl, mode: 'http' | 'browser' }[]`, recorded for every real network page fetch (`web_fetch` and each `web_search` inline fetch).
  - `budgetExhaustions`: `Map<BudgetLimit, { firstTool, skippedReads }>`.
  - `browserLaunches`: integer, incremented by a counting provider decorator.
  - `searchProviders`: distinct provider names in first-use order.
  - Methods: `recordToolOutcome`, `recordSourceFailure`, `recordFetch`, `recordBudgetExhaustion`, `recordBrowserLaunch`, `briefFacts(): { notices: BriefNotice[]; searchProvider: string | null }`, `summary(snapshot, limits, noticeCount): RunHealth`.
- **`RunHealth`** (protocol Zod schema, `packages/protocol/src/schemas/run-health.ts`; persisted as `<runDir>/run-health.json`):
  - `schema_version` (literal `1`)
  - `run_id` (string, NOT NULL)
  - `searches`: `{ total, ok, failed_by_code: Record<string, int>, providers: string[] }`
  - `fetches`: `{ total, by_mode: { http, browser }, repeat_fetches, failed_by_code: Record<string, int> }`. `repeat_fetches` counts network fetches of a normalized URL already fetched in this run. FEAT-050 drives it to 0 and adds `cache_hits` additively.
  - `source_failures`: `{ fetch, extract, blocked, budget, policy }` (int each)
  - `browser`: `{ launches }`
  - `budgets`: `{ navigations_used, navigations_limit, hosts_used, hosts_limit, exhausted: BudgetLimit[] }`
  - `tool_failures`: `{ total, by_code: Record<string, int> }`
  - `notices` (int): count of runtime-derived notices attached to the published document, 0 when nothing was published.

### Protocol changes (additive; Brief schema stays `0.2`)

- `BriefNotice.kind` gains `search_failed`. Old Briefs remain valid.
- `UsageCall.provider` widens from the closed `anthropic | ollama | openai` enum to `z.string().min(1)`. The model registry already admits `google`, `groq`, `mistral`, `openrouter`, and `xai` ([`config/schema.ts:32-40`](../../../packages/core/src/config/schema.ts#L32-L40)). With a closed enum, recording a turn for those providers would make `UsageLedger.parse` throw. Every old value stays valid.
- New `RunHealth` schema, exported with JSON Schema generation like the other artifact schemas.

### Core type changes (internal API; clean breaks permitted)

- `SourceFailure.stage`: `'fetch' | 'extract' | 'blocked'` → adds `'budget' | 'policy'`.
- `AskEthicsGate.checkUrl` decision union adds `{ ok: false; reason: 'budget'; detail; limit: BudgetLimitName }` and `{ ok: false; reason: 'policy'; detail; code: string }`, kept distinct from `BlockedReason` (ethics reasons only). `processSource` maps these to the stages of the same name.
- `rankReasonForFailureStage` returns `DomainRankReason | null`, with `null` for `budget` and `policy`. Every caller skips the signal on `null`.
- `ProcessedSource` gains `fetchMode: 'http' | 'browser' | null`, null when no network fetch happened.
- `UrlPolicyRejection` gains `budgetLimit?: 'navigations' | 'hosts'`, set only for `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`.
- New `sanitizeStructured(value, profile, options?)` in `packages/core/src/sanitizer/` returns `{ value, transformationsApplied, truncated }`.

### Relationships

- One run has exactly one `RunHealthLedger`, zero or one `run-health.json`, and zero or one `run_health` runtime event. Startup failures before the environment exists write neither.
- One tool call has exactly one `toolOutcomes` entry and, when it failed, exactly one `tool_failure` warn line.
- One published document receives `briefFacts()` exactly once, at publish time.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `RunHealth` counts are non-negative integers. `searches.total = ok + Σ failed_by_code`.
- Runtime-derived notices are capped at 10 per document. Overflow becomes one `other` notice that points to `report.md` → Run Health.
- `ToolFailureDiagnostic.cause` must match a declared vocabulary per tool, enforced by a test.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Make the stable audit projection JSON-safe without weakening redaction

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - **Root cause.** In `strippers.ts`, change `URL_IN_TEXT_RE` to `/https?:\/\/[^\s"'<>\\]+/gi`. A backslash is never a legal unescaped URL character, so stopping at it also fixes the model-visible copy's false rewrites (`…/10160610212631779//`) and the hit count they inflated.
  - **Structural fix.** Add `sanitizeStructured(value, profile, options)` in `sanitizer/structured.ts`:
    - Walk JSON-compatible values. Apply the profile's redactors (not its truncation) to every string leaf with the same `preserve` shielding.
    - When a string leaf trimmed-starts with `{` or `[` and `JSON.parse`s to an object or array, sanitize it recursively and re-serialize it with `JSON.stringify`. Pi's `content[].text` is exactly this case.
    - Enforce the profile byte cap structurally: when the serialized result exceeds it, shorten the longest string leaves (UTF-8-safe, with a `…[truncated]` marker) until it fits, and set `truncated`. Never cut the serialized text.
    - Non-JSON input (functions, bigint, cycles) degrades to `sanitize(String(...))` exactly as `coercePayload` does today.
  - In `event-map.ts`, make `createDefaultPiEventMapContext().sanitizePayload` call `sanitizeStructured(payload, 'authenticated')` and return `.value`. Its output is then always structured, and the "emit the text when re-parse fails" branch is deleted.
  - The middleware's model-visible `sanitizeAndBound` path is unchanged. It sanitizes a singly-encoded payload and was never corrupted.
  - Side effect to verify: the orchestrator's `toolMetadata` reads the same projected `event.output`. A stringified output was silently hiding `error_code`/`budget_limit` on those calls, and this fix restores both.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Property test (`fast-check`): arbitrary nested objects whose string leaves mix URLs ending at JSON-escape boundaries (`\"`, `\\`, `\n`), JSON-in-string leaves two levels deep, and canary values (email, SSN, card, phone, API-key shape, `token=` query). After `sanitizeStructured`:
    - `JSON.stringify(result.value)` re-parses;
    - every string-in-JSON leaf that parsed before still parses;
    - no canary survives anywhere (recursive scan);
    - non-canary URLs are byte-identical apart from sanitizer-intended query stripping.
  - A regression fixture replays the exact `web_search` result shape from run `20260925T130634Z` (`…/dallas-tx/` inside double-encoded `content[].text`) through `mapPiEvent` and asserts `tool_finished.output` is an object with a parseable `content[0].text`.
  - Truncation test: an oversized payload stays valid JSON and is marked truncated.
  - `strippers.spec.ts`: a URL followed by `\"` is rewritten without consuming the backslash.
  - Orchestrator test: a `web_search` success whose text contains such a URL still yields `metadata.status === 'ok'` in `toolMetadata`.

- [ ] **Implementation**:

    | Condition                                                                                                          | `errorCode`                   | `retryable` | `cause`                                                                        |
    | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
    | `ScrapeSearchError` code `anomaly-challenge`                                                                       | `SEARCH_BLOCKED`              | false       | `anomaly-challenge`                                                            |
    | `RateLimitError` (HTTP 429)                                                                                        | `SEARCH_BLOCKED`              | false       | `rate-limited`                                                                 |
    | `ScrapeSearchError` code `empty-results`                                                                           | `SEARCH_NO_RESULTS`           | true        | `empty-results`                                                                |
    | `ScrapeSearchError` code `TimeoutError`, or any `SearchProviderError` whose code names a timeout                   | `SEARCH_TIMEOUT`              | true        | `timeout`                                                                      |
    | `ScrapeSearchError` code `ethics-refused:<reason>:…`                                                               | `SEARCH_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | false       | `ethics-refused:<reason>` (detail dropped)                                     |
    | `SearchProviderKeyMissingError`, `NoSearchProviderAvailableError`, `UnknownSearchProviderError`, `TavilyAuthError` | `SEARCH_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | false       | `key-missing` / `no-provider-available` / `unknown-provider` / `auth-rejected` |
    | `SearchProviderError` with `statusCode >= 500`                                                                     | `SEARCH_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | true        | `http-5xx`                                                                     |
    | `SearchProviderError` other (4xx, `parse-error:*`, `invalid-shape`)                                                | `SEARCH_FAILED`               | false       | `http-4xx` / `invalid-response`                                                |
    | `mapBrowserStartupError(error) !== null` (SERP browser will not start)                                             | the FEAT-047 browser code     | false       | `browser-startup`                                                              |
    | anything else                                                                                                      | `SEARCH_FAILED`               | false       | `unexpected:<ErrorClass>`                                                      |

### TASK-005: Runtime-derived Brief notices and `metadata.search_provider`

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Protocol: add `search_failed` to `BriefNotice.kind`, with its `.describe()` updated.
  - `RunHealthLedger.briefFacts()` derives notices deterministically, in this order, capped at 10 with one overflow `other` notice:
    1. **Search failures**: one notice per failing `web_search` code (including `TOOL_TIMEOUT` on `web_search`). Kind `search_failed`, source `search:<provider>` (or `search` when unknown), reason from a fixed per-cause phrase table, e.g. `9 of 22 web searches failed: the provider served an anti-bot challenge (SEARCH_BLOCKED).`
    2. **Budget exhaustion**: one notice per exhausted limit. Kind `budget_exhausted`, source `runtime`, reason `Yantra's navigation budget (30) was exhausted; 4 further page reads were not attempted.` The wording attributes the limit to Yantra, never to a site.
    3. **Per-source read failures**: one notice per `(kind, host)`, merging `web_search` source failures and `web_fetch` failures. `fetch` → `fetch_failed`, `extract` → `extract_failed`, `blocked` → `blocked`, `policy` → `other` with the reason prefixed `Yantra's URL policy refused …`. The reason carries the count and the first stable reason, and never a page path or query.

    `searchProvider` is the distinct provider names joined by `, ` in first-use order, or `null` when no search ran.

  - `PublishToolDeps.publish` options gain `runtimeFacts?: { notices: readonly BriefNotice[]; searchProvider: string | null }`.
    - `createBriefPublisher` appends `runtimeFacts.notices` after any existing notices, including the runtime-assembly notice, and sets `metadata.search_provider` on both the agent-content and complete-Brief paths.
    - `createTemplatedReportPublisher` does the same instead of hardcoding `notices: []` / `search_provider: null`.
  - `result_publish` passes `services.runHealth.briefFacts()`. `maybeAssembleUnpublishedResult` passes the same.
  - The notice count used in TASK-006 comes from the published document, not recomputed.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. No credential, consent, or keychain path changes. `SEARCH_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` for `key-missing` relays setup advice to the user, and the agent gains no capability.
- **Error Handling**: Typed causes are mapped at the nearest tool boundary (search mapper, FEAT-047 browser mapper). Unknown exceptions on `web_search` become residual `SEARCH_FAILED` with an `unexpected:<Class>` cause; on other tools they still reach the middleware's generic `TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED`. No new `catch {}` without a stable code, a log, or a `swallow-ok` justification (enforced by TASK-003). `retryable` is `true` only where an identical or reformulated call can plausibly succeed within the run. Every message names only engineered moves (memory → Coding Standards).
- **Logging**: Pino JSONL in `runtime.jsonl`:
  - `tool_failure` at `warn`, one per failed call;
  - `run_health` at `info`, once at teardown;
  - the FEAT-047 `tool_unexpected_failure` stays at `error`.

  Payloads carry closed codes and causes, a provider name, or a hostname only. Never a message, stack, URL path or query, tool params, page text, or snippet.

- **Security and privacy**: `sanitizeStructured` applies the identical profile to every leaf, including JSON-in-string leaves. A property test asserts both re-parse and canary redaction (plan §6). The goal echo redacts before printing. Runtime-derived notice reasons are built from fixed phrase tables plus counts and hostnames, never page text, so no untrusted string enters the Brief through this path.
- **Ranking**: Only site-caused failures (`fetch`, `extract`, ethics `blocked`) produce negative signals. Budget and URL-policy refusals are Yantra's own and produce none.
- **Compatibility**: The Brief stays at schema `0.2`. All protocol changes are additive or widening, and old Briefs, usage ledgers, and run directories validate and render unchanged. `run-health.json` is optional for every reader.
- **Diagnostic cost**: All facts are recorded from data already in hand at the chokepoint. No extra page read, fetch, or browser call is added. The launch counter is a pass-through decorator.
- **Testing**: Vitest AAA, real exported error classes, `@no-llm` tags on safety and deterministic suites, and per-package targeted runs (`cd packages/<pkg> && npx vitest run …`). Rebuild core and protocol before trusting agent or CLI results. The repo-wide lint/typecheck/e2e run is the final gate.
